[codex] CODEXRELOGIN-01: `hq broker relogin codex` runs the whole recovery and sends the operator the device code (#8129)

## Summary

Adds an attended, end-to-end Codex recovery command that prints and pages the device link/code, then publishes and verifies the recovered grant through the fleet. The operator only needs to approve the device code.



## What changed

Adds oauth_broker.relogin and hq broker relogin codex [--check-only]. Recovery backs up admin credentials, uses bounded device login and the existing Sentinel page channel, loads/kicks the root mirror, waits for file agreement and both brokers' Codex can_serve, syncs as runtime owner, compares worker/broker access hashes and runs an ephemeral smoke. Noninteractive sudo identifies unavailable user switching without prompting. Updates RUNBOOK-broker-ops.md and permanent-refresh failure pages; adds fake-binary recovery tests and page-text regression coverage. No CI checks, gates, config keys or workflows added.

Claude-code follow-up would need bridge-owner login (rather than Codex device auth), the Claude keychain/bridge publication path, Claude-specific credential inspection and worker token consumption, plus Claude broker readiness and smoke verification. This PR implements only Codex.


## Why it matters

The 2026-10-11 SEV0 left Codex unavailable for 69 minutes and recovery required rediscovering the credential publication and worker-sync sequence. Builds on PR 8106, PR 8108 and PR 8109. Operator: "The needs to NEVER HAPPEN AGAIN" and "Auth is THE essential service of the OS". When recovery initially waited for intervention, the operator said: "You have the tools you don't need operator intervention. It has been done before." This command starts recovery and delivers the approval request directly, while keeping upstream refresh tokens out of worker files and out of output.


## Post-merge activities

Normal main-catchup deployment makes the hq command available. Deploy the updated watchdog through its documented operator restart path so future permanent-refresh pages name the recovery command. No live recovery or restarts were performed by this worker.

Stand-in Codex/launchctl/pager/sync binaries and temporary fake auth/log files verify order, repeatability, failure stops, timeout handling, noninteractive user switching, no-op check-only, token redaction and safe mirror-direction reporting; stand-in HTTP broker covers serving Codex despite aggregate HTTP 503. Ruff check/format, git diff --check and shellcheck gate passed. Initial managed push correctly rejected stale CLI reference; regenerated the reference and its parity test passes. No full worker-pool suite or live auth/page/service operations. Managed exact-head push succeeded with budget-deferred attestation after its two automatic budget overruns; GitHub CI and AMA must be green before merge.

[codex] ROLLGUARD-01: a broker roll is announced, waits out a refresh, and is verified provider by provider (#8130)

## Summary

Deploy broker recreates now record both brokers before and after, wait for observed refresh activity to settle, announce the roll on the existing ledger event surface, and verify serving providers and grant times. A failed verification pages with the exact difference, preserves the standby, and suppresses subsequent automatic recreates.



## What changed

Main-catchup owns the roll wrapper and deploy record, with a 300-second quiet-window wait budget and a 120-second post-command verification budget; individual status probes are bounded to five seconds. Both launcher recreate paths use it. Image-drift convergence recreates only the primary, leaving the standby running. Additive broker /readyz fields expose per-grant refresh time and hash prefix, refresh ages, and in-flight refresh observations including direct credential leases. The session-ledger event allowlist registers the two announcements using existing phases and statuses. Image equality repairs the persisted drift receipt. No config.yaml keys, CI checks, ratchets, override labels, or new fail-closed auth conditions were added.

Limits: timing uses status observations; a refresh can start between the last observation and recreate, so this is not an atomic refresh reservation. The reported unavailability duration is explicitly an upper bound from recreate start to verification. A pre-upgrade broker has no grant-status fields: its initial empty grant snapshot cannot prove grant continuity, and the native standby must load the additive status code before subsequent rolls have complete grant evidence on both instances. These limitations are recorded in the walkthrough rather than presented as stronger guarantees.


## Why it matters

The 2026-10-11 SEV0 showed that a silent deploy could load a rolled-back grant while workers were in flight. Operator, verbatim: "The needs to NEVER HAPPEN AGAIN" and "Auth is THE essential service of the OS". This complements PR 8106 (grant-aware mirror), PR 8108 (broker grant monotonicity), and PR 8109 (auth paging and builder holds), with deploy evidence and provider-by-provider outcome verification. The existing grant store remains the protection against an actual rollback; this change makes the deployment and any observed regression visible.


## Post-merge activities

The deploy of this pull request rolls the broker. Normal main-catchup propagation activates the wrapper and primary status fields; use the normal operator-managed standby activation path for its additive status fields, while preserving standby service during primary rolls. No config migration is needed. After a failed verification, investigate and recover the exact provider/grant difference before removing the failed roll record to re-enable automatic rolls. No live host actions were performed by this worker.

## Ticket
ROLLGUARD-01

## Spec
none

## Completion shape
pr

## Risk class
(unset)

## Acceptance evidence

14 scoped main-catchup tests passed (roll and image drift); 76 broker auth-file/token-cache unit tests passed in the declared test environment; one fake-provider /readyz integration test passed (47 unrelated endpoint tests deselected). Launcher and broker-image-drift shell tests returned zero; the existing completion guard records its known CLZ-01 skip for the launcher suite tail. Ruff lint/format, shellcheck gate, docs linkcheck and git diff --check passed. Tests used temporary directories, fake credentials/providers, and stubbed alert seams. Managed git-safe push accepted the final head as budget-deferred after its built-in retry; GitHub CI and AMA still gate merge.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared, opt-in prompt refusal for the reached installer chain.
+installer_unattended_init() {
+  case "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" in
+    0) return 0 ;;
+    1) ;;
+    *) printf 'unattended-input: AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE must be 0 or 1\n' >&2; return 64 ;;
+  esac
+  set +x +v
+  export AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 NONINTERACTIVE=1 CI=1 GH_ASSUME_YES=1
+  export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  export SUDO_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/false
+  # Ignore a supplied interactive SSH command: unattended cannot inherit an agent
+  # or password prompt. Host verification remains enabled.
+  export GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -oIdentityAgent=none -oBatchMode=yes -oConnectTimeout=15 -oServerAliveInterval=15 -oServerAliveCountMax=3'
+  export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_UPGRADE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_CLEANUP=1

+}
+
+installer_unattended_sudo_check() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  [[ "$(id -u)" == 0 ]] && return 0
+  command sudo -n true || {
+    printf 'unattended-input: pre-authorized noninteractive sudo required\n' >&2
+    return 77
+  }
+}
+
+# Functions preserve attended argv exactly. Export only in unattended mode so
+# reached Bash helpers also refuse askpass. sudo policies still authorize every
+# operation; a cached timestamp is never treated as an enduring grant.
+installer_unattended_functions() {
+  [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" == 1 ]] || return 0
+  sudo() {
+    local arg args=()
+    for arg in "$@"; do
+      [[ "$arg" == -A ]] || args+=("$arg")
+    done
+    command sudo -n --preserve-env=AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE,GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT,GIT_ASKPASS,SSH_ASKPASS,GIT_SSH_COMMAND,GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS,GIT_AUTHOR_NAME,GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL,GIT_COMMITTER_NAME,GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL,SUDO_ASKPASS "${args[@]}"
+  }
+  git() {
+    local identity=()
+    if [[ -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME:-}" && -n "${AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL:-}" ]]; then
+      identity=(-c "user.name=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_NAME" -c "user.email=$AGENT_OS_INSTALL_GIT_EMAIL")
+    fi
+    command git "${identity[@]}" -c credential.helper= -c core.askPass=/usr/bin/false \

+# Only idempotent provisioning operations belong here. Unknown and structural
+# failures stop immediately; a transient signature never overrides an auth,
+# permission, certificate-verification or configuration error in the same run.
+installer_output_is_transient() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if grep -Eiq 'permission denied|operation not permitted|authentication failed|could not read (username|password)|repository .*not found|repository not found|host key verification failed|certificate verify failed|certificate verification failed|unable to get local issuer certificate|self.signed certificate|invalid (argument|configuration|plist)|no such file or directory|EACCES|EPERM|E401|E403' "$@"; then
+    return 1
+  fi
+  if [[ "$kind" == runtime ]] && grep -Eiq 'bootstrap failed: 5: input/output error|(^|[^[:alnum:]_])EIO([^[:alnum:]_]|$)|resource temporarily unavailable|service not yet bootstrapped' "$@"; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  grep -Eiq 'timed out|timeout|ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|EAI_AGAIN|connection reset|connection refused|temporary failure in name resolution|could not resolve host|could not resolve hostname|TLS handshake|SSL.*(connect|handshake)|early EOF|remote end hung up unexpectedly|HTTP[^[:digit:]]+50[234]|(error|response|returned)[^[:digit:]]+50[234]' "$@"
+}
+
+installer_run_with_retry() {
+  local kind="$1"
+  shift
+  if [[ "${AGENT_OS_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}" != 1 ]]; then
+    "$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  local capture_dir attempt status delay
+  capture_dir="$(mktemp -d)" || return 1
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    status=0
+    "$@" >"$capture_dir/stdout" 2>"$capture_dir/stderr" || status=$?
+    cat "$capture_dir/stdout"
+    cat "$capture_dir/stderr" >&2
+    if [[ "$status" == 0 ]]; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    if [[ "$attempt" == 3 ]] || ! installer_output_is_transient "$kind" "$capture_dir/stdout" "$capture_dir/stderr"; then
+      rm -rf "$capture_dir"
+      return "$status"
+    fi
+    # Fixed provisioning policy, matching the launchd post-bootout recovery
+    # window. No exponential arithmetic or retry tuning inputs to duplicate.
+    case "$attempt" in 1) delay=2 ;; 2) delay=5 ;; esac
+    printf 'unattended-retry: %s transient failure on attempt %s/3; retrying in %ss\n' "$kind" "$attempt" "$delay" >&2
+    sleep "$delay"
+  done
+}

+    # installer log, but leave a mode-0600 file for the invoking operator.
+    if diagnostics:

+            mode="w", prefix="agent-os-precheck-", suffix=".stderr", delete=False
+        ) as diagnostic_file:

+    ["bash", str(root / "scripts/pre-bootstrap-checklist.sh"), "--json"],

+print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "qualified": coverage.qualified,

+from __future__ import annotations

+import argparse
+import errno
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+import urllib.error
+import urllib.request
+import uuid
+from pathlib import Path

+from agent_os_config.backoff import bounded_exponential_delay
+from agent_os_core.subprocess_retry import transient_error

+QUIET_SECONDS = 120
+WAIT_SECONDS = 300
+VERIFY_SECONDS = 120
+POLL_SECONDS = 2
+COMMAND_ATTEMPTS = 3
+
+
+def _transient_command_error(exc):
+    if isinstance(exc, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
+        return exc.returncode == errno.EIO or transient_error(
+            exc.stderr,
+            ("operation now in progress", "cannot connect to the docker daemon"),
+            (r"bootstrap failed: 5\b",),
+        )
+    return isinstance(exc, OSError) and exc.errno in {errno.EIO, errno.EAGAIN, errno.EBUSY}
+
+
+def _recreate(command):
+    # Keep command diagnostics without a pipe that can hide successful progress.
+    with tempfile.TemporaryFile(mode="w+", encoding="utf-8") as stderr:
+        try:
+            return subprocess.run(command, check=True, timeout=310, stderr=stderr, text=True)
+        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
+            stderr.seek(0)
+            exc.stderr = stderr.read()
+            raise
+        finally:
+            stderr.seek(0)
+            sys.stderr.write(stderr.read())
+            sys.stderr.flush()
+
+
+def snapshot(url):
+    try:
+        response = urllib.request.urlopen(url + "/readyz", timeout=5)
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
+        response = exc  # A 503 still carries provider and grant evidence.
+    with response:
+        body = json.load(response)
+    return {
+        "provider_states": body.get("provider_states", {}),
+        "grants": body.get("grants", {}),
+        "refresh_in_flight": body.get("refresh_in_flight", False),
+    }
+
+
+def _serving_providers(states):
+    return {
+        provider
+        for body in states.values()
+        for provider, state in body.get("provider_states", {}).items()
+        if state.get("can_serve")
+    }
+
+
+def _standby_preflight(states):
+    standby = states.get("standby", {})
+    if not standby or standby.get("observationError"):
+        return ["standby: status observation unavailable"]
+    if not _serving_providers({"standby": standby}):
+        return ["standby: no serving providers observed"]
+    return [
+        f"standby provider {provider}: cannot cover primary during recreate"
+        for provider in sorted(_serving_providers(states))
+        if not standby.get("provider_states", {}).get(provider, {}).get("can_serve")
+    ]
+
+
+def differences(before, after):
+    result = []
+    serving = _serving_providers(before)
+    for broker, previous in before.items():
+        current = after.get(broker, {})
+        if current.get("observationError"):
+            result.append(f"{broker}: status observation unavailable")
+            continue
+        for provider in serving:
+            if not current.get("provider_states", {}).get(provider, {}).get("can_serve"):
+                result.append(f"{broker} provider {provider}: can_serve true -> false/missing")
+        for grant, state in previous.get("grants", {}).items():
+            new = current.get("grants", {}).get(grant, {})
+            if new.get("last_refresh", -1) < state["last_refresh"]:

+v1.88.2 ServiceLogging.async_log_success_event drops the request timestamps
+and parent. Legacy OpenTelemetry converts those timestamps before checking

+Our watchdog exercises this path every 60 seconds via its chat probe.
+Request hooks and parented service spans remain owned by upstream OpenTelemetry.
+"""

+
+

+    async def async_service_success_hook(
+        self,
+        payload,
+        parent_otel_span=None,
+        start_time=None,
+        end_time=None,
+        event_metadata=None,
+    ):
+        if parent_otel_span is None:
+            return
+        await super().async_service_success_hook(
+            payload=payload,
+            parent_otel_span=parent_otel_span,
+            start_time=start_time,
+            end_time=end_time,
+            event_metadata=event_metadata,
+        )
+

+        event_metadata=None,

+        if parent_otel_span is None:

+        from opentelemetry import trace
+        from opentelemetry.trace import Status, StatusCode
+
+        _start_time_ns = 0
+        _end_time_ns = 0
+        if isinstance(start_time, float):

+        else:

+            )

+            )
+            if event_metadata:

+        end_time=None,
+        event_metadata=None,
+    ):
+        from opentelemetry import trace
+        from opentelemetry.trace import Status, StatusCode
+
+        _start_time_ns = 0
+        _end_time_ns = 0
+        if isinstance(start_time, float):
+            _start_time_ns = int(int(start_time) * 1000000000.0)
+        else:
+            _start_time_ns = self._to_ns(start_time)
+        if isinstance(end_time, float):
+            _end_time_ns = int(int(end_time) * 1000000000.0)
+        else:
+            _end_time_ns = self._to_ns(end_time)

+            _span_name = payload.service
+            service_logging_span = self.tracer.start_span(

+                context=trace.set_span_in_context(parent_otel_span),

+            )

+            self.safe_set_attribute(
+                span=service_logging_span, key="service", value=payload.service.value
+            )
+            if error:
+                self.safe_set_attribute(span=service_logging_span, key="error", value=error)

+        - Adds Otel as a service callback

+            return

+        if getattr(proxy_server, "open_telemetry_logger", None) is None:
+            setattr(proxy_server, "open_telemetry_logger", self)

+        try:

+                duration=_duration,
+                call_type=kwargs.get("call_type", "unknown"),
+            )

+
+class RecoveryError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class CommandError(RecoveryError):
+    """Keep only classification flags, never raw command output, in exceptions."""
+
+    def __init__(self, message, *, transient=False, service_absent=False):
+        super().__init__(message)
+        self.transient = transient
+        self.service_absent = service_absent

+
+def command(name, default):
+    return shlex.split(os.environ.get(name, default))

+def run(argv, timeout=30):
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(
+        argv,
+        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+        start_new_session=True,
+    )
+    try:
+        output, _ = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+        if proc.returncode:
+            diagnostic = output.decode(errors="replace").lower()
+            raise CommandError(
+                "command failed; check permissions and service logs",
+                transient=any(
+                    marker in diagnostic
+                    for marker in (
+                        "input/output error",
+                        "bootstrap failed: 5:",
+                        "resource temporarily unavailable",
+                        "timed out",
+                        "timeout",
+                    )
+                ),
+                service_absent=any(
+                    marker in diagnostic
+                    for marker in (
+                        "could not find service",
+                        "could not find specified service",
+                        "service not found",
+                        "no such process",
+                    )
+                ),
+            )
+        return output
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        raise CommandError(
+            "command timed out; inspect service logs and retry", transient=True
+        ) from None
+    finally:
+        try:
+            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        except ProcessLookupError:

+        proc.wait()
+
+
+def run_launchctl(argv, *, allow_absent=False):
+    """Retry only known transient launchd errors, at most three 30-second attempts."""
+    for attempt in range(3):
+        try:
+            run(argv)
+            return True
+        except CommandError as exc:
+            if allow_absent and exc.service_absent:
+                return False
+            if not exc.transient or attempt == 2:
+                raise
+            time.sleep(bounded_exponential_delay(attempt, base_seconds=1, max_seconds=2))

+def fingerprint(path, *, user=None):
